name: Ariel Jain
life: “I still remember reading a will before I understood what I liked doing.” On Wednesday, near the foot of Harbor Viaduct, Ariel pauses where the machinery overhead makes two people stand close enough to hear each other.
voice: I am the child who loves both parents and has no interest in inheriting their chair at the bank.
appearance: Ariel has full cheeks and a mouth that pulls slightly to one side. Look for a swept fringe and a closely clipped nape. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a boxy denim jacket with a watch on a cracked leather band. In conversation Ariel leans a shoulder against the wall during long conversations.
personality: Ariel loves a well-told anecdote and distrusts the neat ending. The parts Ariel remembers are the interruptions, unfinished jobs and people who had to go back to work halfway through.
agenda: To decline the inherited management chair gracefully.
family: Rosa Taylor is Ariel’s second cousin. Ariel offers the first invitation. Rosa gets to change the plan. They learned that a promise to visit is easier to keep when changing a time does not count as letting down the whole family. Asked about *The empty chair on nights*, Rosa says, “I am her neighbor. I can deliver soup but I refuse to carry gossip in either direction.”
connections: Charles Shah. Unpaid parental work explains why the adult child sees inheriting the chair as an obligation. Also in the story is Magdalena Macrae (parent).
